content.content:
1	---
2	title: "Bundled templates"
3	description: "All 23 ready-made graphics in Frame Job, what each one draws, how long it runs, and every property you can change."
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
9	
10	Frame Job comes with 23 ready-made motion graphics: titles, pointers for screencasts, social pieces, charts and timers. Insert one, fill in its text and colours, and it's an ordinary graphic clip that you can change as far as you like.
11	
12	<AtAGlance
13	  menu="Insert ▸ Graphic…"
14	  where="Clip tab ▸ Graphic sub-tab ▸ Properties"
15	  tools={['list_graphics', 'insert_graphic']}
16	/>
17	
18	## The bundled templates
19	
20	The **Insert ▸ Graphic…** dialog lists the templates under four categories. An **overlay** is transparent, so whatever is on the tracks below shows around it. A **card** fills the whole frame and hides what's below.
21	
22	| Template | Category | Kind | Default length | At 30 fps |
23	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
24	| [Arrow highlight](#arrow-highlight) | Screencast | Overlay | 90 frames | 3 s |
25	| [Bar chart](#bar-chart) | Data & Time | Card | 150 frames | 5 s |
26	| [Callout](#callout) | Screencast | Overlay | 90 frames | 3 s |
27	| [Chapter card](#chapter-card) | Titles & Text | Card | 120 frames | 4 s |
28	| [Countdown](#countdown) | Data & Time | Overlay | 330 frames | 11 s |
29	| [Counter](#counter) | Data & Time | Overlay | 90 frames | 3 s |
30	| [Donut chart](#donut-chart) | Data & Time | Card | 150 frames | 5 s |
31	| [End screen](#end-screen) | Social & YouTube | Card | 300 frames | 10 s |
32	| [Gauge](#gauge) | Data & Time | Overlay | 120 frames | 4 s |
33	| [Handle tag](#handle-tag) | Social & YouTube | Overlay | 120 frames | 4 s |
34	| [Keyboard keys](#keyboard-keys) | Screencast | Overlay | 90 frames | 3 s |
35	| [Kinetic type](#kinetic-type) | Titles & Text | Card | 150 frames | 5 s |
36	| [Line chart](#line-chart) | Data & Time | Card | 150 frames | 5 s |
37	| [Logo reveal](#logo-reveal) | Titles & Text | Card | 120 frames | 4 s |
38	| [Lower third](#lower-third) | Titles & Text | Overlay | 150 frames | 5 s |
39	| [News ticker](#news-ticker) | Titles & Text | Overlay | 300 frames | 10 s |
40	| [Progress bar](#progress-bar) | Data & Time | Overlay | 120 frames | 4 s |
41	| [Quote card](#quote-card) | Titles & Text | Card | 150 frames | 5 s |
42	| [Social popup](#social-popup) | Social & YouTube | Overlay | 120 frames | 4 s |
43	| [Step badge](#step-badge) | Screencast | Overlay | 90 frames | 3 s |
44	| [Subscribe button](#subscribe-button) | Social & YouTube | Overlay | 150 frames | 5 s |
45	| [Title card](#title-card) | Titles & Text | Card | 120 frames | 4 s |
46	| [Window frame](#window-frame) | Screencast | Overlay | 150 frames | 5 s |
47	
48	## Insert a template
49	
50	<Steps>
51	
52	1. Move the playhead to where the graphic should start.
53	
54	2. Choose **Insert ▸ Graphic…**, then a category, then a template. The preview plays it on a loop at your project's canvas shape.
55	
56	3. Choose **Insert**, press <kbd>Return</kbd>, or double-click the template.
57	
58	</Steps>
59	
60	The clip lands at the playhead, on the front track when it fits there, and otherwise on a new track above everything else. [Insert a graphic](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/) has the whole dialog.
61	
62	## Change what a template shows
63	
64	Select the clip and open the **Graphic** sub-tab of the **Clip** tab. **Properties** has one row for each property the template offers, under the template's own short name, such as **boxWidth**. A number with a range is a slider and a field, a number without one is a field, a yes-or-no choice is a checkbox and a fixed set of choices is a pop-up.
65	
66	<Shot
67	  name="07-clip-graphic.inspector"
68	  alt="The Graphic sub-tab for a Lower third. Properties lists Title as Jane Doe, subtitle as Director of Photography, an orange accent swatch, a size slider at 64, a ticked boxed checkbox and an align pop-up set to left."
69	/>
70	
71	See [Graphic properties](/graphics/properties/) for how the rows behave, and [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/) to change a value over time.
72	
73	## How long a template runs
74	
75	The default length is in frames at your canvas's frame rate, so a 150-frame template is 5 seconds in a 30 fps project and 2.5 seconds in a 60 fps one.
76	
77	You can make the clip longer or shorter. With **Follow Clip** on, as it is on a new clip, the exit moves with the clip's end, and the entrance plays from the first frame as before. A few templates also time something else by the clip's length:
78	
79	| Template | What follows the clip's length |
80	| --- | --- |
81	| Counter | Reaches its final number about 70 % of the way through. |
82	| Progress bar | Reaches its value about 60 % of the way through. |
83	| Subscribe button | The first click lands 40 % of the way through. |
84	
85	[Countdown](#countdown) and [News ticker](#news-ticker) run in real time whatever the clip's length. See [Graphic size and timing](/graphics/size-and-timing/) for pinning a graphic's own timeline.
86	
87	## Titles & Text
88	
89	### Chapter card
90	
91	A card with a large outlined chapter number, a kicker beside it, an accent rule drawing across and the title rising into view.
92	
93	| Property | What it does | Default |
94	| --- | --- | --- |
95	| **number** | The chapter number, 0 to 99, always shown as two digits. | 1 |
96	| **kicker** | The small text beside the number. It wraps to at most three lines. | CHAPTER |
97	| **title** | The title under the rule, fitted to the width. | Getting started |
98	| **background** | The card's colour. | `#0b0b10` |
99	| **accent** | The number's outline and the rule. | `#ff5a36` |
100	
101	### Kinetic type
102	
103	A sentence shown word by word, each word springing in, on a near-black card. Every fifth word, counting from the fourth, takes the accent colour.
104	
105	| Property | What it does | Default |
106	| --- | --- | --- |
107	| **text** | The sentence. | Make something people want to watch twice, then cut it in half |
108	| **stagger** | Frames between one word and the next, 1 to 30. | 4 |
109	| **color** | Most of the words. | `#ffffff` |
110	| **accent** | The fourth word, the ninth, the fourteenth and so on. | `#ffd60a` |
111	
112	The sentence wraps at 80 % of the canvas's width, at one fixed size, and centres on the frame. A long one can run off the top and bottom, so split it across two clips. The card's colour isn't a property.
113	
114	### Logo reveal
115	
116	A card on which an accent bar sweeps across, revealing your logo or a text mark. The bar then settles into a short rule, and a tagline fades up under it.
117	
118	| Property | What it does | Default |
119	| --- | --- | --- |
120	| **logo** | A picture to reveal. **None** draws the **mark** instead. | None |
121	| **mark** | The text to reveal when there's no picture, fitted to the width. | FRAME JOB |
122	| **tagline** | The line under the rule. Leave it empty for none. | Edit at the speed of thought |
123	| **background** | The card's colour. | `#0b0b10` |
124	| **accent** | The bar and the rule. | `#ff5a36` |
125	
126	The **logo** pop-up lists the pictures added to the project's graphics, so add yours first with **File ▸ Add Image to Graphics…**. See [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/). The picture keeps its proportions inside a box half the width of the title-safe area.
127	
128	### Lower third
129	
130	A name and a subtitle that slide in from the left and fade out, on a dark bar with an accent edge.
131	
132	| Property | What it does | Default |
133	| --- | --- | --- |
134	| **Title** | The name. | Jane Doe |
135	| **subtitle** | The line under it. | Director of Photography |
136	| **accent** | The bar at the left edge. | `#ff5a36` |
137	| **size** | The size of the name, 12 to 200. The subtitle is half of it. | 64 |
138	| **boxed** | Draws the dark box behind the text. The accent bar stays either way. | On |
139	| **align** | Puts the whole block `left`, `center` or `right`. The text inside it stays left-aligned. | `left` |
140	
141	The box grows to fit the longer line, and the text isn't shrunk to fit. A long name at a large **size** can run off the frame.
142	
143	### News ticker
144	
145	A band along the foot of the frame with a headline box at its left and items crawling right to left, with an accent dot between them. Type the items in one field, separated by a vertical bar (`|`). They repeat for as long as the clip runs.
146	
147	| Property | What it does | Default |
148	| --- | --- | --- |
149	| **headline** | The text in the box. Leave it empty for no box. | BREAKING |
150	| **items** | The items, separated by a vertical bar. | Three sample lines |
151	| **speed** | How fast they crawl, 40 to 600, in pixels a second when the canvas's shorter side is 1080, and in proportion on others. | 160 |
152	| **background** | The band's colour, slightly see-through. | `#101014` |
153	| **accent** | The headline box, the band's top edge and the dots. | `#e5322d` |
154	
155	### Quote card
156	
157	A card with a large quote mark, the quote's lines fading up in turn, and a short rule and the attribution sliding in.
158	
159	| Property | What it does | Default |
160	| --- | --- | --- |
161	| **quote** | The quote, in a text area. | Good editing is invisible. All anyone should notice is the story. |
162	| **attribution** | Who said it, drawn after a dash. Leave it empty for no name. | The Editor |
163	| **background** | The card's colour. | `#101014` |
164	| **accent** | The quote mark and the rule. | `#ffd60a` |
165	
166	The quote shrinks and wraps to fit the frame. It wraps by itself, so line breaks you type are treated as spaces.
167	
168	### Title card
169	
170	A title fitted to the frame with a kicker above it, over a diagonal two-colour gradient. The text fades in and rises, then fades out over the last 18 frames, and the gradient stays.
171	
172	| Property | What it does | Default |
173	| --- | --- | --- |
174	| **title** | The title, fitted to 80 % of the canvas's width. | The Long Road to a Motion Graphic |
175	| **kicker** | The small line above it. | CHAPTER ONE |
176	| **from** | The gradient's top-left colour. | `#1b2a6b` |
177	| **to** | The gradient's bottom-right colour. | `#c2185b` |
178	
179	## Screencast
180	
181	### Arrow highlight
182	
183	Points at something on a screen recording: a rounded box drawn on around a spot, an arrow growing toward it from the side nearer the frame's centre, and a label at the arrow's tail.
184	
185	| Property | What it does | Default |
186	| --- | --- | --- |
187	| **x**, **y** | The spot, as a fraction of the frame's width and height, 0 to 1. | 0.62, 0.42 |
188	| **boxWidth**, **boxHeight** | The box's size, as a fraction of the frame, 0.02 to 0.8. | 0.22, 0.14 |
189	| **shape** | `box+arrow`, `box` or `arrow`. | `box+arrow` |
190	| **label** | The text. Leave it empty for none. | Look here |
191	| **accent** | The box and the arrow. | `#ffd60a` |
192	
193	With `box` the label sits under the box, or above it when there's no room. With `arrow` the arrow points at the spot itself and the two box sizes do nothing. The box, arrow and label are always kept inside the title-safe area, so a spot near the edge is moved in.
194	
195	### Callout
196	
197	A circle that draws itself round a spot, with an arrow and a label.
198	
199	| Property | What it does | Default |
200	| --- | --- | --- |
201	| **x**, **y** | The circle's centre, as a fraction of the frame's width and height, 0 to 1. | 0.62, 0.4 |
202	| **label** | The text at the arrow's tail. | Click here first |
203	| **color** | The circle and the arrow. | `#ff3b30` |
204	
205	The arrow always comes from the lower left, and nothing keeps it on the frame. Near the left or bottom edge the arrow and label run off, so use [Arrow highlight](#arrow-highlight) there.
206	
207	### Keyboard keys
208	
209	A shortcut drawn as keycaps that pop in one after another and are then pressed in turn, with a label under them.
210	
211	| Property | What it does | Default |
212	| --- | --- | --- |
213	| **keys** | The keys, joined by `+`. | cmd+shift+4 |
214	| **label** | The line under the keys. Leave it empty for none. | Screenshot a selection |
215	| **theme** | `light` or `dark` keycaps. | `light` |
216	| **position** | `bottom`, `center` or `top`. | `bottom` |
217	| **accent** | The small bar on each keycap. | `#ff5a36` |
218	
219	The names in **keys** can be in any case:
220	
221	| Type | To draw |
222	| --- | --- |
223	| `cmd`, `command` or `⌘` | ⌘ |
224	| `shift` or `⇧` | ⇧ |
225	| `opt`, `option`, `alt` or `⌥` | ⌥ |
226	| `ctrl`, `control` or `⌃` | ⌃ |
227	| `up`, `down`, `left`, `right` | An arrow |
228	| `plus` | The + key |
229	| One character | That character, in capitals |
230	| Anything longer, such as `esc` | That word on a wider keycap |
231	
232	A long row of keys shrinks to fit the frame. A clip needs at least 25 frames plus 10 for each key to press them all before its exit, so a shortcut of seven or more keys wants longer than the default 90 frames.
233	
234	[Shortcut overlays](/recording/shortcut-overlays/) places clips drawn by this template for you, from the shortcuts in a screen recording.
235	
236	### Step badge
237	
238	A numbered accent circle popping in at a corner, with a label panel wiping out from behind it.
239	
240	| Property | What it does | Default |
241	| --- | --- | --- |
242	| **number** | The step's number, 0 to 99. | 1 |
243	| **label** | The panel's text. Leave it empty for no panel. | Open the export sheet |
244	| **position** | `top-left`, `top-right`, `bottom-left` or `bottom-right`. | `top-left` |
245	| **accent** | The circle. | `#ff5a36` |
246	
247	### Window frame
248	
249	A browser or app window's frame to sit over a screen recording: a title bar with three dots, a title or an address field, and a rounded outline. The inside stays clear.
250	
251	Put the recording on a track below the frame, then use the [Picture tab](/canvas/picture-tab/) to fit it inside the outline.
252	
253	| Property | What it does | Default |
254	| --- | --- | --- |
255	| **style** | `browser` draws back and forward arrows and an address field. `window` draws a title. | `browser` |
256	| **title** | The title, shown with the `window` style. | Frame Job |
257	| **url** | The address, shown with the `browser` style. | example.com |
258	| **theme** | `dark` or `light`. | `dark` |
259	| **scale** | The share of the title-safe area the frame covers, 0.5 to 1. | 0.86 |
260	| **shadow** | Draws a soft shadow outside the outline. | On |
261	| **accent** | The address field's outline, so it has no effect with `window`. | `#ff5a36` |
262	
263	The shadow is only as wide as the room around the frame, so it thins out as **scale** nears 1.
264	
265	## Social & YouTube
266	
267	### End screen
268	
269	A card laid out for a video's end screen: a title, two 16:9 spaces and a subscribe circle. On a landscape or square canvas the two spaces sit side by side with the circle centred under them. On a portrait canvas they're a column.
270	
271	| Property | What it does | Default |
272	| --- | --- | --- |
273	| **title** | The line at the top. Leave it empty for none. | Watch next |
274	| **videoA** | The label under the first space. | Latest video |
275	| **videoB** | The label under the second space. | Best for you |
276	| **subscribe** | The label under the circle. | Subscribe |
277	| **background** | The card's colour. | `#0b0b10` |
278	| **accent** | The play buttons and the circle's outline. | `#ff5a36` |
279	
280	The spaces are placeholders drawn into the picture, for the video elements you add on the platform when you publish. They don't link to anything.
281	
282	### Handle tag
283	
284	An accent tile holding a glyph, with a pill showing your @handle expanding from behind it, at a corner.
285	
286	| Property | What it does | Default |
287	| --- | --- | --- |
288	| **handle** | The text in the pill. Leave it empty for no pill. | @framejob |
289	| **glyph** | `play`, `camera`, `bubble`, `note` or `globe`. | `play` |
290	| **position** | `bottom-left`, `bottom-right`, `top-left` or `top-right`. | `bottom-left` |
291	| **accent** | The tile. | `#ff5a36` |
292	
293	### Social popup
294	
295	A notification card rising in at a corner, with a generic avatar and a handle. Its heart, speech bubble or share arrow pops as the count ticks up by one.
296	
297	| Property | What it does | Default |
298	| --- | --- | --- |
299	| **kind** | `like` draws a heart, `comment` a speech bubble and `share` an arrow. | `like` |
300	| **handle** | The name on the card. | @framejob |
301	| **text** | The comment. It shows only with `comment`, at most three lines, and anything further is dropped. | Loved this edit! |
302	| **count** | The number it starts from, 0 or more. It ends one higher. | 1280 |
303	| **position** | `bottom-right`, `bottom-left`, `top-right` or `top-left`. | `bottom-right` |
304	| **accent** | The heart, bubble or arrow. | `#ff3b30` |
305	
306	### Subscribe button
307	
308	A button that a cursor glides to and clicks. It turns grey with a check and its done label, then a bell pops in beside it and rings after a second click.
309	
310	| Property | What it does | Default |
311	| --- | --- | --- |
312	| **label** | The button before the click. | SUBSCRIBE |
313	| **doneLabel** | The button after it. | SUBSCRIBED |
314	| **bell** | Adds the bell and the second click. | On |
315	| **position** | `bottom`, `center` or `top`. | `bottom` |
316	| **accent** | The button before the click, and the bell once it's clicked. | `#e5322d` |
317	
318	## Data & Time
319	
320	The three charts read their data from text fields, with entries separated by commas:
321	
322	- Values and labels pair up by position, and a value with no label has a blank one.
323	- An entry that isn't a number is dropped, so the values after it line up one label earlier.
324	- An empty entry, such as a comma at the end, counts as 0.
325	
326	### Bar chart
327	
328	Bars growing one after another on a dark card, each with its figure above it and its label below, under a title.
329	
330	| Property | What it does | Default |
331	| --- | --- | --- |
332	| **values** | The bars' values, separated by commas. | 12, 19, 7, 24, 15, 30 |
333	| **labels** | The labels, separated by commas. | Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat |
334	| **title** | The line at the top. It isn't fitted, so keep it short. | Sessions per day |
335	| **color** | The bars. | `#2d7ff9` |
336	
337	The tallest bar sets the scale, and the figures are rounded to whole numbers. The card's colour isn't a property.
338	
339	### Countdown
340	
341	A timer counting down or up, one step a second, inside a ring that empties or fills. The digits pulse on each tick, and the circle flashes in the accent colour at the end.
342	
343	| Property | What it does | Default |
344	| --- | --- | --- |
345	| **from** | The starting number, in seconds. | 10 |
346	| **to** | The final number. Make it greater than **from** to count up. | 0 |
347	| **format** | `seconds` shows 90, `m:ss` shows 1:30 and `h:mm:ss` shows 0:01:30. | `m:ss` |
348	| **label** | The line above the digits, drawn in capitals. | Starting in |
349	| **ring** | Draws the ring. Without it the digits stay on their dark disc. | On |
350	| **accent** | The ring and the flash. | `#ff5a36` |
351	
352	The count runs in real seconds whatever the frame rate, so the clip's length decides how far it gets. The default 330 frames is 11 seconds at 30 fps, which fits a ten-second count and the exit. At 60 fps that clip is 5.5 seconds, so lengthen it. For any longer count, lengthen the clip to the count plus a second.
353	
354	With **from** and **to** equal there's nothing to count: the number stands in a full ring and nothing flashes.
355	
356	### Counter
357	
358	A number counting from one value to another with thousands separators, a prefix and a label under it. It starts fast and slows into its final number, then holds.
359	
360	| Property | What it does | Default |
361	| --- | --- | --- |
362	| **from** | The starting number. | 0 |
363	| **to** | The final number. | 1284093 |
364	| **prefix** | Text right before the number. | $ |
365	| **label** | The line under it. | raised this year |
366	| **color** | The number and the label. | `#f5f5f0` |
367	
368	The number shows no decimals, and it isn't shrunk to fit, so a very long one can run past the edges.
369	
370	### Donut chart
371	
372	Slices sweeping round a donut on a dark card, with the first slice's share counting up in the centre above its label, and a legend with each share. The legend sits beside the donut on a landscape or square canvas, and below it on a portrait one.
373	
374	| Property | What it does | Default |
375	| --- | --- | --- |
376	| **values** | The slices' values, separated by commas. A value below 0 counts as 0. | 45, 30, 15, 10 |
377	| **labels** | The labels, separated by commas. | Video, Audio, Graphics, Other |
378	| **title** | The line at the top. | Where the time goes |
379	| **accent** | The first slice. | `#ff5a36` |
380	
381	The other slices take colours from a fixed set of six, in order, repeating after the sixth. The shares are rounded to whole percentages, so they may not add up to exactly 100. The card's colour isn't a property.
382	
383	### Gauge
384	
385	A 270° dial with ticks, whose accent arc and needle swing to a value while the figure counts up.
386	
387	| Property | What it does | Default |
388	| --- | --- | --- |
389	| **value** | The reading, held between **min** and **max**. | 72 |
390	| **min** | The start of the dial. | 0 |
391	| **max** | The end of the dial. At or below **min** it's taken as **min** plus 1. | 100 |
392	| **label** | The line inside the dial, drawn in capitals. | Speed |
393	| **units** | The line under the figure. | km/h |
394	| **accent** | The arc and the needle. | `#ff5a36` |
395	
396	A whole **value** counts in whole numbers, and any other shows one decimal place.
397	
398	### Line chart
399	
400	A line drawn on through its points on a dark card, a dot popping at each one, with the last value called out in a pill.
401	
402	| Property | What it does | Default |
403	| --- | --- | --- |
404	| **values** | The points, separated by commas. | 12, 18, 15, 26, 22, 34, 41 |
405	| **labels** | The labels along the bottom, separated by commas. | Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr, May, Jun, Jul |
406	| **title** | The line at the top. | Monthly active users |
407	| **area** | Shades the area under the line. | On |
408	| **accent** | The line, the dots' outlines, the shading and the pill. | `#2d7ff9` |
409	
410	The scale runs from 0, or from the lowest value if that's negative, up to the highest. A single value draws one dot and no line. The card's colour isn't a property.
411	
412	### Progress bar
413	
414	A labelled bar on a dark plate, filling to a percentage with the figure counting, and a shine sweeping across it once it has filled.
415	
416	| Property | What it does | Default |
417	| --- | --- | --- |
418	| **value** | How far it fills, 0 to 100. | 68 |
419	| **label** | The text above the bar. | Rendering |
420	| **showPercent** | Shows the percentage at the right. | On |
421	| **position** | `bottom`, `center` or `top`. | `bottom` |
422	| **accent** | The fill. | `#2d7ff9` |
423	
424	## Any canvas shape
425	
426	Templates size themselves by the shorter side of the canvas, so nothing grows too large on a tall project.
427	
428	Seventeen of them are laid out for all three shapes. Everything they draw stays inside the title-safe area, the frame less 5 % on every side, at every frame at 1920 × 1080, 1080 × 1920 and 1080 × 1080. Their entrances are a spring, a wipe or a fade, and never a move in from outside the frame. Long text is fitted or wrapped to stay inside, down to a smallest size for each text, so a paragraph typed where a title belongs can still run over.
429	
430	The other six are Bar chart, Callout, Counter, Kinetic type, Lower third and Title card. They don't keep to the title-safe area, and a Lower third enters from beyond the frame's left edge. With their default text, their words sit at least 24 pixels inside a 1080 × 1920 frame. Only Title card fits its title and Kinetic type wraps its text, so check your own words on a tall canvas. [Safe areas](/canvas/safe-areas/) shows the title-safe guide in the preview.
431	
432	A square canvas takes the landscape layout.
433	
434	## Templates end clean
435	
436	The same seventeen each have an accent colour and leave in about their last 15 frames, so the last frame is bare. An overlay ends clear, and a card ends on its background alone. A card's background never animates: only what's on it moves or fades.
437	
438	The other six end their own way:
439	
440	| Template | At the end of the clip |
441	| --- | --- |
442	| Lower third | Fades out over the last 15 frames and ends clear. |
443	| Title card | Its text fades over the last 18 frames, leaving the gradient. |
444	| Bar chart, Callout, Counter, Kinetic type | Hold to the last frame and stop with the clip. |
445	
446	## Template fonts and glyphs
447	
448	Templates draw only with fonts that come with Frame Job, so a project looks the same on any Mac. The font isn't a property. To change it, [edit the graphic's code](/graphics/edit-a-module/).
449	
450	| Used for | Font |
451	| --- | --- |
452	| Text in most templates | Montserrat, extra bold or black |
453	| Digits that tick, and the figures in Bar chart | IBM Plex Mono |
454	| Window frame's title and address | Source Sans 3, semibold |
455	| Title card's title | Anton |
456	| Title card's kicker and Bar chart's labels | Bebas Neue |
457	| Callout's label | Darker Grotesque |
458	
459	Every symbol is a generic shape drawn by the template, never a brand's artwork: the keycap symbols, the heart, the bell, the play triangle and the glyphs in Handle tag. None of them is a platform's own logo.
460	
461	## Good to know
462	
463	- Each insert copies the template into the project under a free name, such as `lower-third`, then `lower-third-2`. Undo takes the clip away, and the copy stays until you [delete it](/graphics/manage-graphics/).
464	- Your copy is yours to change, and it stays as it was when you inserted it. [Graphics in a vertical version](/graphics/vertical-graphics/) covers the one exception.
465	- An action can't change these properties, which keep one value for the whole clip: **number** in Chapter card and Step badge, **values** and **labels** in Donut chart and Line chart, **keys** in Keyboard keys, **items** in News ticker and **count** in Social popup.
466	
467	## Related
468	
469	- [What a graphic is](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/)
470	- [Insert a graphic](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/)
471	- [Graphic properties](/graphics/properties/)
472	- [Write a graphic module](/graphics/write-a-module/)
473

46:## Adding a graphic
47-
48-**Insert ▸ Graphic…** opens the Graphic dialog. On the left are the
49-categories: **This Project** first, when the project's `graphics/` folder
50-holds a module (every module in it, whatever its own category), then the
51-bundled templates' categories, in alphabetical order. In the middle are the
52-chosen category's graphics, by name. On the right a preview plays the chosen
53-graphic over a checkerboard, looping, at the project's canvas shape, with its
54-name and a one-line description under it. A module that doesn't compile is
55-listed in grey and its preview is the red error card.
56-
57-The dialog opens on the first category's first graphic. **Insert** (Return,
58-or a double-click on a graphic) adds the chosen graphic; **Cancel** (Esc)
59-closes the dialog; **From File…** closes it and asks for a `.js` module to
60-copy into the project instead, or a `.fjgraphic` to import (see
61-[Sharing a graphic](#sharing-a-graphic)). **Export…**, at the far left, saves the chosen
62-graphic to share (see [Sharing a graphic](#sharing-a-graphic)).
63-
64-A module of your own goes into a category by giving its `meta` a `category`
65-(and a `description` for the line under the preview); one without a category
66-is listed under **Other**, last (see the [graphics reference](../graphics-api.md)).
67-
68-The bundled templates:
69-
70-| Template | Category | What you get | Default length |
71-|---|---|---|---|
72-| Arrow highlight | Screencast | A rounded box drawn on around a spot, an arrow growing toward it from the side nearer the frame's centre, and a label at the arrow's tail | 90 frames |
73-| Bar chart | Data & Time | A titled bar chart whose bars grow in turn, from comma-separated values and labels | 150 frames |
74-| Callout | Screencast | A circle that draws itself on, with an arrow and a label, at a position on the frame | 90 frames |
75-| Chapter card | Titles & Text | A full-frame card: a large outlined chapter number, a kicker, an accent rule drawing across and the title rising into view | 120 frames |
76-| Countdown | Data & Time | A timer counting down (or up) one step a second inside a ring that empties or fills, pulsing on each tick and flashing at the end | 330 frames |
77-| Counter | Data & Time | A number counting from one value to another with thousands separators, a prefix and a label | 90 frames |
78-| Donut chart | Data & Time | A titled donut whose slices sweep in turn from comma-separated values and labels, the first slice's share counting up in the centre, with a legend beside it (below it in portrait) | 150 frames |
79-| End screen | Social & YouTube | A full-frame card with a title, two 16:9 placeholders for the videos you link, side by side, and a subscribe circle centred under them (a column in portrait) | 300 frames |
80-| Gauge | Data & Time | A dial with ticks whose accent arc and needle swing to a value, with the value counting up and its units and label | 120 frames |
81-| Handle tag | Social & YouTube | An accent tile holding a generic glyph (play, camera, speech bubble, note or globe) and a pill with your @handle, at a corner | 120 frames |
82-| Keyboard keys | Screencast | A shortcut such as cmd+shift+4 as keycaps popping in, each pressed in turn, with ⌘ ⇧ ⌥ ⌃ and the arrows drawn as symbols, and a label under them | 90 frames |
83-| Kinetic type | Titles & Text | A sentence shown word by word, each word springing in, with an accent colour | 150 frames |
84-| Line chart | Data & Time | A titled line drawn on through comma-separated values, a dot popping at each point, an optional area fill and the last value called out | 150 frames |
85-| Logo reveal | Titles & Text | A full-frame card on which an accent bar sweeps across, revealing your logo image (or a text mark), then becomes a rule over a tagline | 120 frames |
86-| Lower third | Titles & Text | A name and subtitle that slide in and fade out, boxed or not, aligned left, centre or right | 150 frames |
87-| News ticker | Titles & Text | A band along the foot of the frame with a headline box and items, separated by "\|", crawling right to left | 300 frames |
88-| Progress bar | Data & Time | A labelled bar on a plate whose fill grows to a percentage, the figure counting, with a shine across it, at the bottom, centre or top | 120 frames |

  they fit a tall frame and draw exactly as before on a landscape or square

Inserting a template:

1. Copies the module into the project's `graphics/` folder under a free name
   (a second Lower third becomes `lower-third-2`, and so on). The two then
   show under This Project as "Lower third — lower-third" and "Lower third —
   lower-third-2".
2. Places one graphic clip at the playhead, on the front track if it fits
   there, otherwise on a new track above everything. With a nest open, the
   clip goes on the nest's front track, or a new track inside the nest.
3. Selects the new clip so the inspector shows its Graphic sub-tab.

Inserting a graphic from **This Project** places a clip drawn by that module
